# 06 Parse nested control-flow blocks (loop, alt/else, opt, par/and, critical/option, break, rect)

## Outcome

`parseSequenceDiagram` recognizes all seven Mermaid control-flow block forms, nested to arbitrary
depth: `loop ... end`, `alt ... else ... end` (any number of `else` branches), `opt ... end`,
`par ... and ... end` (any number of `and` branches), `critical ... option ... end` (any number of
`option` branches), `break ... end`, and `rect rgb(...)/rgba(...) ... end`. Each produces a
recursive `SequenceStatement` block node containing its nested body/branches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the seven block keywords parses standalone, wrapping one or more messages, into the
  matching `SequenceStatement` block kind with the body statements nested inside.
- [ ] `alt is sick \n ... \n else is well \n ... \n end` parses to one `alt` node with two
  branches, each carrying its condition label (`is sick`, `is well`) and body.
- [ ] `par ... and ... and ... end` (two `and` branches, three total) parses to one `par` node
  with three branches.
- [ ] `critical ... option ... option ... end` parses analogously to `par`/`alt`.
- [ ] `rect rgb(191, 223, 255) ... end` and `rect rgba(0,255,0,0.1) ... end` both parse, carrying
  the raw color string through unvalidated (rendering ticket 09 is responsible for using it as an
  SVG fill).
- [ ] Blocks nest: a `loop` containing an `alt` containing a `par` parses to the correctly nested
  tree, three levels deep.
- [ ] A block missing its `end` returns `document: null` plus an error diagnostic; does not throw.
- [ ] Blocks freely interleave with plain messages and participant/create/destroy statements
  (create/destroy parsing itself isn't required yet — ticket 11 adds that — but a block containing
  only plain messages alongside blocks at the same nesting level must parse correctly).
